The gate is currently ratcheting `packages/fields` on a verdict computed from a catch block — that is a gate-machinery defect, not polish. Fix shape is named (JSONC/TS parser + round-trip-every-tsconfig assertion); the one embedded question (whether `fields` stays in the specifier leg once parsed) is small enough to surface in the PR.

Fold ruling: **FOLD with #5382** — see the five-gate answer recorded on #5382; this card is the second member, claim goes on the chain head.

`main` has moved `60d452ee` → `7d0143c3` since dispatch, so the branch is also stale. **Delete it or reset it from current `main`; ⛔ do not branch on top of it.**

### Carried forward so the next dispatch does not re-derive it

Verified on `origin/main` `60d452ee` — **re-check against current `main` `7d0143c3` before relying on any of it**, but this is where to start:

- `readTsconfig` is still the three-regex strip at `:124-130`; `effectiveNoEmit` still answers from its `catch` at `:145-150`.

- ⇒ **The triage FOLD-with-#5382 ruling is moot, not unexecuted.** #5382 landed alone. Treat this as a standalone remainder; ⛔ do not hunt for a fold partner.
- The card's claim that `ts.parseConfigFileTextToJson` adds no new dependency edge (because #5382 made `typescript` reachable from the shared scanner) was **not** independently verified by me — verify before relying on it.
- Note this file imports from `./check-phantom-dependencies.mjs`; shared-helper changes reach further than this gate.

Concurrent in this batch: #3840 (`apps/console` probe) and #5458 (`eslint-rules/` + app-shell views) — neither touches `scripts/`.

## ⛔ Two dead branches precede you. Do not build on either.

This card has been claimed twice and delivered zero times, both times by devs that died silently:

- `claude/issue-5367-readtsconfig-jsonc` — exists on the remote, **0 commits of its own**, stale at `60d452ee`. ⛔ **Do not branch from it, do not reset it, do not reuse its name.** Branch from current `main` under the new name above.
- The prior claim (`5365444185`) was released by its own session with evidence. Nothing is owed to it.

The reason both are recorded rather than swept: a dev that correctly *stops* also has zero commits, and the two are indistinguishable under `git`. The deciding reading was the absent report comment, not the empty branch. Same standard applies to you — **if you stop, say so in a report**; silence will be read as death.

## Premise re-verified on `origin/main` @ `2074a59`, all four readings

⛔ Not inherited. Measured now:

| reading | result |
|:--|:--|
| `readTsconfig` is still the regex strip | **yes** — `:124`, three `.replace()` calls over raw text, then `JSON.parse` |
| `parseConfigFileTextToJson` in that file | **0** |
| positive control on the same file (`effectiveNoEmit`) | **3** — so the zero above is a real zero, ⛔ not a bad path |
| the two poisoned configs still carry `/*` inside JSON strings | **yes** — `packages/auth/tsconfig.json:9` `"@/*": ["src/*"]` and `:37` `"**/*.test.ts"`; `packages/fields/tsconfig.json:7` (`packages/*/src` inside a `//` comment) and `:33` |

And `#5382`'s landed code still points here, at `:91` and `:404`: *"is a SEPARATE live instance of the same class — objectui#5367"*.

**The triage FOLD-with-#5382 ruling is moot, not unexecuted** — #5382 landed alone and named this as its remainder. ⛔ Do not hunt for a fold partner.

## The embedded question — ⛔ must not be answered silently

Parsed correctly, `effectiveNoEmit` returns **true** for `packages/fields`, which drops it **out** of the specifier leg of the ratchet. Today it is inside that leg only because the parse throws and the `catch` grades it "emitting".

So the fix necessarily changes a gate's scope. Both of these are acceptable; **exactly one thing is not**:

- keep `fields` in scope deliberately, and say in the PR body why and how;
- let it drop out, and report that as a **named consequence** with the measurement behind it;
- ⛔ let the scope change land unremarked. That is the failure this card exists to end — a verdict nobody computed.

The card's own measurement, which you should re-confirm rather than inherit: `fields`' `dist` carries **0** extensionless relative specifiers even before #5214's fix; its published entry failed through `@object-ui/providers`, never on its own file.

## The assertion this class of bug needs

Whatever the parse strategy, ship the check that would have caught it: **`readTsconfig` round-trips every tsconfig in the repository without throwing.** Cheap, and it is the difference between fixing two files and closing the class.

## PM mechanism assumptions — verify, do not trust

1. `ts.parseConfigFileTextToJson` is the natural fix and the repo already depends on `typescript`. The previous seat explicitly recorded that it did **not** verify the "adds no new dependency edge" claim. **Verify it yourself** before relying on it — `scripts/` has its own dependency discipline and `check:phantom-deps` will have an opinion.
2. A string-aware hand-rolled strip is the fallback if 1 fails. Weaker: it is the same category of code as the bug.
3. This file imports from `./check-phantom-dependencies.mjs` — shared-helper changes reach further than this one gate. Check what else consumes anything you touch there.

## Premise-first

The issue body is a lead, not a specification. `premise_still_valid: false` with no PR is a legitimate delivery if the tree has moved under it — though the four readings above say it has not. Read the card and all four of its comments on GitHub yourself, and **check the body for sanitizer truncation** before relying on it.
